The best option depends on your study level, academic record, work experience and financial circumstances. This guide helps you compare the strongest opportunities, understand what they actually pay for and focus on scholarships that fit your profile.

Here’s the thing: the biggest scholarship is not automatically the scholarship you are most likely to win.

Take a Nigerian graduate with a first-class degree but only six months of post-degree employment. The academic profile may be excellent, yet the applicant would not meet Chevening’s work-experience rule. A merit-based university scholarship could be a much better target.

Start with eligibility. Then write the application.

Fully Funded UK Scholarships for Nigerian Students

For applicants who need support beyond a partial tuition discount, these are the strongest opportunities to investigate.

1. Chevening Scholarship 2027/28

Chevening is one of the best-known fully funded UK scholarships for Nigerian students pursuing a one-year taught Master’s degree.

The official Chevening application timeline confirms that applications opened on 4 August 2026 and close at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026. Successful scholars begin their studies in September or October 2027.

Work experience is one of the biggest filters.

You need at least 2,800 hours of eligible work experience gained after completing your undergraduate degree. Full-time work, part-time employment, voluntary work and eligible paid or unpaid internships can count. Chevening explains the calculation in its work-experience guidance.

Applicants also need an undergraduate degree that qualifies them for a UK Master’s programme and must select three eligible courses.

You do not need an unconditional university offer when submitting the initial scholarship application. Successful candidates must later provide at least one unconditional UK university offer by 8 July 2027.

Chevening is therefore a strong option for an experienced graduate.

It is not an undergraduate scholarship.

2. Rhodes Scholarship for West Africa

For Nigerian applicants targeting postgraduate study at Oxford, Rhodes is one of the most important current opportunities.

The West Africa application window opened on 1 June 2026 and closes at 23:59 GMT on 27 August 2026.

Rhodes covers Oxford University course fees and provides a living stipend. At the latest published rate, the stipend is £20,400 per year, or £1,700 per month.

That makes it materially different from a tuition-only award.

A student who wins a £15,000 fee discount may still need substantial money for accommodation and living costs. Rhodes addresses much more of the actual cost of studying at Oxford.

3. Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship

The current Commonwealth Master’s guidance still shows the 2026/27 application cycle as closed.

That does not mean the scholarship is unavailable permanently. It means 2027 applicants should wait for the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission to publish the new application window rather than relying on predicted dates.

The latest published financial package is substantial. It includes approved tuition fees, return airfare and a living allowance currently set at £1,712 per month, or £2,000 per month for scholars studying at universities in the London metropolitan area.

A study-travel grant and certain other allowances may also apply.

Applicants normally need at least a UK-equivalent 2:1 degree. A 2:2 may qualify when accompanied by an appropriate postgraduate qualification. Candidates must also demonstrate that they could not otherwise afford to study in the UK.

Another point applicants sometimes miss: the CSC does not simply select candidates from direct applications alone. Commonwealth Master’s applications involve approved nominating bodies, and those organisations can operate their own selection procedures.

If this scholarship matches your profile, prepare your documents and development-impact case now, then confirm the 2027/28 dates once the CSC releases them.

4. Gates Cambridge Scholarship

Gates Cambridge offers full-cost scholarships to exceptional postgraduate applicants from outside the UK.

The programme awards roughly 75 full-cost scholarships each year, with the majority available through the international application round.

5. PTDF Overseas Scholarship

Nigerian MSc and PhD applicants in energy and related technical disciplines should also monitor the Petroleum Technology Development Fund.

The latest PTDF overseas scheme supported study at selected partner universities in the UK and other countries.

  • Return flight tickets
  • Health insurance
  • Tuition fees
  • Bench fees where applicable
  • Accommodation allowances
  • Living allowances

The current published scheme relates to 2026, so its deadline should not be recycled as a 2027 deadline.

Applicants should monitor the official PTDF scholarship portal for the next overseas call.

Undergraduate Scholarships for Nigerian Students in the UK

Fully funded undergraduate awards are much less common than postgraduate scholarships.

That catches many applicants by surprise. Search results can contain dozens of pages about “fully funded UK scholarships”, yet many of the headline awards require applicants to have already completed a bachelor’s degree.

Undergraduate students still have worthwhile options.

Reach Oxford Scholarship

Reach Oxford is one of the strongest options for students from eligible low-income countries who cannot study for a suitable degree in their home country because of financial, political or educational circumstances.

  • Course fees
  • A grant towards living costs
  • One return airfare per year

The award normally lasts three or four years depending on the course.

Oxford makes only around two or three awards per year, so competition is exceptionally high.

Applications for 2026 entry are closed. Oxford says details for 2027 entry will be published in January 2027.

There is an important sequence here: you must apply to Oxford and receive an offer before the university can consider you for Reach Oxford.

The university application therefore comes first.

University of Manchester Global Futures Scholarship

Manchester's latest Global Futures awards provide a useful example of the scale of university-funded support available to Nigerian students.

For 2026, eligible African undergraduate applicants, including Nigerians, could receive up to £30,000, normally £10,000 per year over three years.

For eligible African Master’s students, the latest published award is £18,000, deducted from international tuition fees. Nigeria is included among the eligible African countries in the university's current Global Futures information.

These are 2026 figures, not confirmed 2027 amounts.

That distinction is important. Manchester can change eligibility, deadlines or award values for a new cycle.

UK Master’s Scholarships for Nigerian Students

Master’s students generally have the broadest range of UK scholarship options.

Alongside fully funded schemes, partial university awards can reduce tuition substantially and may have different eligibility requirements.

GREAT Scholarships

The British Council's current GREAT Scholarships for Nigeria provide £10,000 towards tuition fees for eligible one-year taught postgraduate courses in the 2026/27 academic year.

Across the wider programme, more than 140 scholarships are offered through over 60 UK universities in 2026/27.

Each university sets its own eligible courses, application method and deadline.

The Nigeria page currently covers 2026/27, so applicants should wait for the 2027/28 list before assuming the same universities will participate again.

Still, £10,000 is a useful planning benchmark.

For an applicant who does not qualify for Chevening, a GREAT award attached to a suitable university offer may be more realistic than spending months pursuing a scholarship whose eligibility rules cannot be met.

Nottingham Developing Solutions Scholarship

The University of Nottingham's Developing Solutions Master's Scholarship offered 50% or 100% of full-time Master’s tuition fees for the 2026 cycle.

It targets international applicants who want to contribute to economic, environmental, structural, social or political development in their home countries.

Applicants must hold an offer for an eligible course.

The 2026 deadline was 15 April 2026. That date is useful as historical context, but it should not be treated as the 2027 deadline.

Wait for Nottingham to publish the next cycle.

Allan and Nesta Ferguson Scholarship at Sheffield

The latest Ferguson Scholarship at Sheffield offered a particularly strong package:

Full tuition fee waiver + £12,500 maintenance stipend

Nigeria was included among the eligible countries for the 2026 scheme.

However, the award applied only to specified development-related Master’s programmes and had additional eligibility conditions.

This is a good example of why scholarship names alone are not enough. You also need to check the eligible course list.

The 2027 scheme should only be treated as confirmed once Sheffield publishes its next terms.

Eligibility for UK Scholarships: What Nigerian Students Need

There is no single eligibility formula for UK scholarships for Nigerian students.

Most applications begin with nationality and academic qualifications. After that, the rules can differ sharply.

Chevening requires at least 2,800 hours of post-degree work experience.

Commonwealth Master’s normally expects at least a 2:1, although a 2:2 plus a relevant postgraduate qualification may meet its academic requirement.

Rhodes applies constituency-specific criteria.

University scholarships can place more weight on academic achievement, the course you choose and the strength of your university application.

Think about it this way.

Eligibility should shape your strategy.

How to Apply for a Scholarship in the UK from Nigeria

Start with the scholarship requirements, not with a generic personal statement.

1. Choose your study level

Separate undergraduate, taught Master’s and PhD opportunities immediately.

It sounds obvious, but doing this removes a surprising amount of irrelevant scholarship information.

2. Build a realistic shortlist

For each award, check:

  • Nigerian eligibility
  • Academic requirements
  • Eligible courses
  • Work-experience rules
  • Application status
  • Deadline
  • Whether you need a university offer first

3. Verify the current application cycle

Do not assume last year's deadline will repeat.

Scholarship providers can change the deadline, eligible universities, award value or application process from one cycle to another.

4. Apply to suitable universities

Some scholarship applications require you to hold an offer before applying.

If you are still working through admission choices, understand the UK application process for international students before finalising your scholarship calendar.

5. Prepare your documents

Common requirements include:

  • Passport or accepted identity document
  • Degree certificate or other academic qualifications
  • Complete transcripts
  • CV or résumé
  • References
  • University offer where required
  • Scholarship essays
  • Work-experience evidence
  • Research proposal for relevant PhD applications

Then write specifically for the scholarship.

Do not send the same essay everywhere.

Chevening looks for evidence around leadership, networking, course choice and career plans. Commonwealth applications focus heavily on development impact.

If your argument still sounds generic, strengthen the motivation and evidence behind your application.

A concrete example is much stronger than a slogan.

“I want to improve healthcare in Nigeria” tells a selector very little.

Explaining the problem you encountered in a specific hospital, what you did about it, what skill you still lack and how the UK degree will help you address that gap gives the selector something real to assess.

UK Scholarships Without IELTS for Nigerian Students

Yes, some Nigerian applicants can pursue scholarships without taking IELTS specifically.

But scholarship requirements and university admission requirements are not always identical.

The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission states in its current Master’s conditions that it does not require candidates to take IELTS.

Your chosen university may still require proof of English proficiency.

Depending on the institution and your academic background, that evidence could include another recognised English test or an accepted alternative.

Before paying for IELTS automatically, check study routes where IELTS may not be required specifically, then confirm the English evidence accepted by your chosen university.

“Without IELTS” does not necessarily mean “without proof of English”.

How Much Can a UK Scholarship Save?

The most useful number is not always the headline scholarship amount.

A GREAT Scholarship currently contributes £10,000 towards tuition.

Manchester's latest African Master’s Global Futures award is £18,000.

Nottingham Developing Solutions can cover 50% or 100% of tuition.

Sheffield's latest Ferguson package combines a full tuition waiver with a £12,500 maintenance stipend.

Fully funded programmes go further.

The current Commonwealth Master’s package includes approved tuition fees, return airfare and a stipend of £1,712 per month, or £2,000 per month in London.

Rhodes' latest published stipend is £20,400 per year, alongside Oxford fees and several other eligible costs.

That difference matters.

A £15,000 tuition discount may look generous, but you could still need to finance rent, food and other living expenses yourself. A scholarship with a lower visible cash figure may leave you financially better off if it covers more categories of expenditure.

Documents Nigerian Applicants Should Prepare

Your checklist will vary by scholarship, but prepare the essentials before deadlines become urgent:

  • Passport or accepted national identification
  • Academic certificates
  • Full academic transcripts
  • CV
  • Reference letters
  • University offer where required
  • Scholarship-specific essays
  • Evidence of work experience where relevant
  • Research proposal for applicable postgraduate research programmes

Do not assume missing documents can always be supplied later.

A technically excellent application can still fail eligibility screening because a required document was missing at the deadline.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the best UK scholarships for Nigerian students in 2027?

Strong options include Chevening, Rhodes West Africa, Commonwealth Master’s, Gates Cambridge, Reach Oxford, PTDF and university awards such as GREAT, Nottingham Developing Solutions and Manchester Global Futures. The right option depends on your level of study, qualifications, work experience and financial needs.

Are there fully funded undergraduate scholarships for Nigerian students in the UK?

Yes, but they are much less common than postgraduate awards. Reach Oxford is one example that can cover course fees, living support and an annual return airfare. Oxford says its 2027 application details will be published in January 2027.

Can Nigerian students get fully funded Master’s scholarships in the UK?

Yes. Chevening and Commonwealth Master’s are major options. Depending on your university and course, other routes can include Rhodes, Gates Cambridge, PTDF and university-funded awards.

Can I get a UK scholarship without work experience?

Yes.

Work experience is not a universal scholarship requirement. Chevening requires at least 2,800 hours of eligible post-degree experience, while many university scholarships focus more heavily on academic performance, nationality, course eligibility and the quality of your application.

Can HND holders apply for UK scholarships?

Sometimes.

University admission and scholarship eligibility are separate. A university may accept an HND for a particular progression route while the scholarship itself requires a different academic profile.

Check both sets of requirements.

Do Commonwealth Scholarships require IELTS?

The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission itself does not require candidates to take IELTS. Your chosen university can still require acceptable evidence of English proficiency.

When should Nigerian students apply for 2027 UK scholarships?

Start preparing now.

Rhodes West Africa closes on 27 August 2026, while Chevening closes on 6 October 2026. Other 2027 scholarship dates will appear as providers publish their new cycles.

Can I apply for more than one UK scholarship?

Usually, yes, during the application stage.

Build a Shortlist That Fits You

There are plenty of UK scholarships for Nigerian students, but applying to everything you find is rarely a good strategy.

Keep checking the dates as the 2027 cycle develops.

The strongest application is not the one sent to the most scholarships.

It is the one sent to the right scholarship, with strong evidence, before the right deadline.
